_comment: MATERIAL CATALOG scene DEFINITION (201F4F51 template-free) - the Component Catalog's sibling for MATERIALS. All 256 slots of the voxel material byte as sixteen rows of sixteen boxes, row-major (a slot's id = row head + column head), with the material's name under each box. Every box is an authored `surface` on this scene's own `mc_sample` stage, its panel the authored well: an ASSIGNED slot's box holds a LIT SPHERE the engine's material-sample filler (flicker-materialview) draws in that material - a promoted bundle's seven maps (package/materials/<id:03>/) when the package holds one, else the flat PBR its index row reads as (its colour, its family's finish, its own colour as Emit for an emissive) - as a POSTER that renders once and re-renders only when its maps arrive or change; a FREE slot gets no sample and shows the well; the top eight slots are held for EMISSIVE materials (Aaron 2026-10-20), show the well and say so. A VIEWING tool: nothing here edits a material - that is the MaterialBench. Every box is PRESSABLE (a click, or a pad Confirm on the box under the cursor): it opens the Material Inspector modal on that slot (scenes/shared/material_inspector.scene.json, hosted by flicker_materialcatalog::MaterialInspector) - the one material on a turning lit sample, its graph read-only, what the package holds for it and its definition. The `materialcatalog` behaviour (flicker-materialcatalog) seats one sample per assigned slot in its box by id and publishes names + tally; materialcatalog.lua derives the emissive block's labels. Display strings are $tokens.

params._comment: The behaviour's own configuration. `sample_map_px` is the edge, in texels, every promoted bundle's maps are decoded to (on the worker pool, square) before its sphere wears them - a box is about 111x35 px at 1080p and a sphere shows half its texture's width at once, so 128 is ample. AARON'S TO TUNE - a placeholder, never a Rust constant. A whole number > 0; anything else is warned and every bundle wears its flat stand-in instead.

mc_sample._comment: The Material Catalog's LIT SAMPLE - every box of the grid is a `surface` naming this stage, and for an ASSIGNED slot the engine's material-sample filler (flicker-materialview) draws that slot's material on a sphere under it. The `material` layer IS that sphere. Every box is a POSTER - `rate: poster` is authored on each surface NODE, because the walker reads liveness off the node, not the stage - so every assigned slot's sphere renders once and keeps its image, and a box re-renders only when its maps arrive (a bundle decoded on the worker) or change. The target clears TRANSPARENT ($stage_void) so the box's authored well (`catalog.well`, the surface's panel) is the backdrop; a free slot (or an emissive slot that holds no row yet) gets no sample and shows the well alone. Lighting and the BLOOM match the MaterialBench's lit stage (`materialbench_lit` - a gate pins the bloom numbers equal), so a material and its glow read the same in both; the FRAMING is deliberately tighter (see `_camera`). EVERY NUMBER HERE IS AN ART PLACEHOLDER, Aaron's to tune in-window, never in Rust.
mc_sample._camera: FRAMING - deliberately TIGHTER than the MaterialBench's (`dist` 2.2 here, 2.6 there). A box is about 111x35 px at 1080p and the camera's field of view is vertical, so at 2.6 the unit sphere would fill only ~0.72 of the box height (~25 px); at 2.2 it fills ~0.9 (~31 px) and still leaves the bloom's halo room above and below. The yaw/pitch are the bench's. AARON'S TO TUNE in-window - a placeholder, never a Rust constant.
mc_sample._emissive_gain: EMISSIVE GAIN - the draw-time multiplier on a material's Emit in this stage's HDR space (the catalog hands it to every sphere's maps). An 8-bit Emit texel caps at 1.0, so at 1.0 a glow never outshines the surface's own white and never crosses the bloom threshold; 4.0 drives an emissive-class row (Lava, and the eight glows in the emissive slots 248-255) past it, so it reads as a glow rather than as paint. The MaterialBench's `materialbench_lit` authors the same 4.0 (a gate holds the two equal). A finite number >= 0 (the stage compiler gates anything else). AARON'S TO TUNE in-window - a placeholder, never a Rust constant. The Emit COLOUR stays the material's own; this is only how bright it burns.
mc_sample._hdr: HDR: the `scene` pass (the lit sphere) renders into the LINEAR rgba16f `hdr` working attachment, `bloom` spreads whatever crosses its threshold (an emissive at the gain above; a hot specular off low-roughness metal) into a halo, and `tonemap_grade` resolves it (ACES roll-off) into the sRGB `color` LAST - the reads/writes ARE the order, no pass numbers anywhere. grade_strength 0 = tonemap only, no invented tint - an art grade is Aaron's to author. Alpha passes through, so the transparent clear the well shows through survives.

passes._comment: BLOOM - what makes an EMISSIVE read as a glow: it reads the linear `hdr` the scene pass wrote, extracts everything above the threshold into a half-res buffer, blurs it, and ADDS the halo back into `hdr` (its coverage as alpha, so it shows past the sphere's edge over the transparent clear) - after the scene pass, before the tonemap. The pocclusters/MaterialBench values, EVERY NUMBER AN ART PLACEHOLDER tuned in-window: `threshold` ~1.0 is the brightness a pixel must exceed to bloom, so a lit matte sphere (< 1.0) does not glow; `knee` the soft shoulder below it; `intensity` how strongly the halo is added back; `radius` the blur spread.

window._comment: This scene's root slab - scene-owned like the other benches' (a shared file would fork the look; duplication is the pattern).

well._comment: Each box's backdrop WELL - the panel of its `surface`, drawn by the walker beneath the composited sphere (the sample clears transparent) and alone in a free or emissive slot.

cell._comment: Each slot's PRESSABLE cell (a `panel` - the standard full-rect control: it flows its well and name like a cell and fires `mc_open_<id>` on a click or a pad Confirm, opening the Material Inspector). RESTING it paints nothing (the transparent fill), so the grid reads exactly as before; HOVERED - the pointer over it - it wears a quiet 1 px neutral rim, the hand's acknowledgement that the box is pressable; FOCUSED - the pad cursor on it - it wears the sapphire focus rim around the box (the cell's 2 px `pad` keeps the rim clear of the well), and focus wins over hover. Aaron's to tune.

nav_footer._comment: Bench nav rail band (like the Component Catalog's). `frame` = the node's own slab; `rule` (top hairline) + `label` (legend ink) + the `pad_glyphs` atlas resolve as the component's defaults.
nav_footer.label: $dim

children._comment: THE GRID PANE - the container the 256 slot cells (`tab_group: mc_panel`) belong to, so the pad's pane tier is clear: the left stick steps between this pane (stop 1) and the footer (stop 2); inside it the d-pad walks the slots AS THE GRID LAYS THEM OUT (`nav: grid` - Down is the slot below, Right the slot beside; past the grid's edge it carries on in id order) and Confirm opens the one under the cursor.

17 columns x 17 rows: a 28px head column and a 14px head row, then the 16x16 slot cells. The heads carry explicit col/row; the cells auto-flow row-major into the free cells, so slot 0 lands at (row 1, col 1) and a slot's id is its row head + column head. Every cell is AUTHORED here, whichever slots the index assigns today: a pressable `panel` (`mc_slot_<id>`, `action: mc_open_<id>` - a click or a pad Confirm opens the Material Inspector on that slot, a FREE slot included; `tab_group: mc_panel` with `nav_ordinal` = id + 1 - the order the pad falls back to past the grid's edge inside the `mc_panel` pane) holding a `surface` (`mc_box_<id>`, `source: mc_sample`, `rate: poster`) whose panel is the well (`style: catalog.well`) - the behaviour seats a lit sample in it for an assigned slot and nothing for a free or emissive one - and a `text` bound to that slot's name.
